rows.name: Chiefs’ Children’s School
rows.note: The boarding school Kamehameha III founded for the children of the aliʻi, run by Amos Starr and Juliette Cooke; a long two-storey frame building where ʻIolani Barracks stand now, ready by 1840. Renamed the Royal School in 1846; its boarding ended in 1850.

rows.name: Kamehameha School for Boys
rows.note: The boys’ school opened in 1887 on the grounds it shared with the Bishop Museum, which took the site over after the school moved up to Kapālama (from 1931).

rows.name: St. Louis College
rows.note: Moved from Āhuimanu in 1881 to Beretania Street beside Washington Place; it moved again in 1883.

rows.name: St. Louis College
rows.note: At Kamakela, on the bank of Nuʻuanu Stream near Chinatown, where College Walk keeps its name, from 1883 until the school opened at Kalaepōhaku in 1928.

rows.name: Sacred Hearts Convent School
rows.note: The boarding and day school beside the Cathedral of Our Lady of Peace from 1859, the academy’s precursor; the record read gives no year it closed here, and the academy at Kaimukī was founded in 1909.

rows.name: Saint Francis School
rows.note: Founded in 1924 by the Sisters of Saint Francis at their convent in Mānoa; it closed in 2019.

rows.name: Hawaiʻi Baptist Academy
rows.note: Opened in 1949 in surplus Army barracks on Heulu Street in Makiki; moved to Nuʻuanu in 1975.

sources.title: School Status and Improvement Reports
sources.author: Hawaiʻi State Department of Education, Office of Strategy, Innovation and Performance (ARCH)
sources.note: Fetched 2026-11-06 from the Department's report repository, one report per school for SY 1999–2000, 2004–05, 2009–10, 2014–15, 2018–19 and 2024–25; the first pages of each read for the school's description (the year it says it opened or was founded, and where it says it moved), its fall enrolment, and in 2024–25 its name as the Department writes it.
sources.wanted: For the schools whose descriptions give no year: the school's own history page, or the Department's school directory, for the year it opened.
